To prevent header injection attacks in C++ code, it is important to properly sanitize user input before using it in headers or other parts of the application that could be vulnerable to injection attacks. Here are some best practices to prevent header injection attacks:

1. Sanitize User Input: Ensure that any user input that is used in headers or other parts of the application is properly sanitized to remove any potentially malicious characters. In the code example provided, the input is sanitized by removing non-printable ASCII characters and trimming leading and trailing whitespace.

2. Validate Input: Validate user input to ensure that it meets the expected format and does not contain any unexpected characters. Use regular expressions or other validation techniques to check for valid input.

3. Encode Output: When outputting user input in headers or other parts of the application, make sure to properly encode the data to prevent injection attacks. Use encoding functions provided by the language or framework to encode special characters.

4. Use Safe APIs: When working with headers or other sensitive parts of the application, use safe APIs provided by the language or framework to handle user input. Avoid using functions that directly concatenate user input with headers, as this can lead to injection vulnerabilities.

5. Limit User Input: Limit the amount of user input that is accepted in headers or other parts of the application to reduce the risk of injection attacks. Set appropriate limits on input length and restrict the types of characters that are allowed.

By following these best practices, you can help prevent header injection attacks in your C++ code and improve the overall security of your application.
